Render a document to Pandoc Markdown

Source: R/render_markdown.R
pub_markdown.Rd

Writes a document (see pub_doc()) as Markdown for pandoc, and its figures as image files. pub_render() uses it for DOCX, PDF and Markdown files. It can also be used to see or post-process the Markdown that pandoc gets.

Usage

pub_markdown(
  doc,
  target = c("docx", "latex", "typst", "md"),
  assets_dir,
  cache = NULL,
  spec = NULL
)

Arguments

doc

A pub_doc.

target

"docx", "latex", "typst" or "md".

assets_dir

Directory for the figure files (created if needed). The Markdown refers to them as <basename(assets_dir)>/figure-<n>.<ext>, so the Markdown file belongs in the parent of assets_dir.

cache

A pub_cache() or NULL (render every figure). Figures are cached as in pub_html().

spec

A pub_report_spec() of the target's format ("pdf" for LaTeX and Typst), or NULL (the default spec of the format).

Value

character(1) Markdown.

Details

Targets

  • "docx": Markdown for pandoc's Word writer. Tables become native Word tables, and caption numbers and the table of contents Word fields. Landscape parts get their own sections and, if the spec locks, tables and figures are locked.

  • "latex", "typst": Markdown for a PDF via xelatex or Typst. Tables are written as LaTeX or Typst code that breaks across pages and repeats the header rows. Figures are PNG images unless the spec's figure asks for "pdf" (LaTeX) or "svg" (Typst).

  • "md": a plain Markdown document with a YAML front matter that holds the header, numbered headings, tables as Pandoc multiline tables and images. Page breaks, landscape parts and tables of contents are left out.

The document header (title, subtitle, author, time) of DOCX is not part of the Markdown. pub_render() passes it to pandoc as metadata.

Texts, widgets and errors

  • Texts are CommonMark (see pub_text()). Raw HTML and pandoc's own syntax in them show as text, as in HTML.

  • Widgets are replaced by their fallback figure (see pub_meta()) or skipped with a warning.

  • Error items (failed steps) are written as marked paragraphs. pub_render() refuses them unless the spec shows them.

  • Cross-references in texts (see pub_text()) become Word cross-reference fields, LaTeX or Typst references or, for "md", the label and number.

Math in PDFs

LaTeX runs TeX commands, so for the "latex" target pandoc's math parser checks every formula first. A formula it can't read, or one that defines macros, is an error.

Report spec

The report spec (see pub_report_spec()) adds the front matter, table of contents, section numbers, caption labels, figure devices and page. pub_render() calls pub_markdown() with its spec. The document's metadata is used as-is (no render-time metadata), so the Markdown of a document is always the same.

See also

pub_render(), pub_html(), pub_report_spec()

Examples

doc <- pub_doc(
    pub_section(
        "Results",
        pub_text("The slope is **negative** ($b < 0$)."),
        pub_table(data.frame(batch = c("A", "B"), slope = c(-0.26, -0.25)),
                  caption = "Slopes", digits = c(slope = 2L))
    ),
    title = "Demo"
)
cat(pub_markdown(doc, "md", assets_dir = tempfile()))
#> ---
#> title: "Demo"
#> ---
#> 
#> # 1 Results
#> 
#> The slope is **negative** ($b < 0$).
#> 
#> Table 1: Slopes
#> 
#> -----------------------
#>  **batch**   **slope** 
#> ----------- -----------
#>  A               -0.26 
#>                        
#>  B               -0.25 
#> -----------------------
